svg.aria-label: What does a fixed-size memory say about Harsh? A timeline: Bob → editor is already stored, then Harsh → admin is written, then much later Harsh → viewer, then the memory is read with the query key Harsh, y = S_t q. Four update rules. Plain linear attention, S_t = S_{t−1} + v_t k_tᵀ, keeps both values under the same key, so the read returns admin + viewer, they interfere. Decay as in RetNet and GLA, S_t = γ_t S_{t−1} + v_t k_tᵀ, returns viewer plus γⁿ times admin, mostly viewer, but Bob → editor fades to γᵐ editor too, it forgets everything a bit. The delta rule of DeltaNet, S_t = S_{t−1} + β_t (v_t − S_{t−1} k_t) k_tᵀ, reads the old value admin at the key and writes only the difference viewer − admin, so it returns viewer and Bob stays intact, it edits just that key. The gated delta rule of Gated DeltaNet and KDA, S_t = α_t S_{t−1} + β_t (v_t − α_t S_{t−1} k_t) k_tᵀ, returns viewer, and the gate α near 1 keeps Bob while α near 0 clears stale memory, edit plus forget. KDA makes α per channel, Diag(α_t). Toy picture with unit orthogonal keys and β = 1.
